stem:
On further questioning of the paramedic crew, they report that when they first arrived on the scene, eyewitnesses said Johnny had been unconscious for 5–10 minutes. When they assessed him, he would open his eyes to verbal stimulus, respond to questions with unintelligible/meaningless words, and localise painful stimulus by pushing their hands away.

Which one of the following was Johnny’s GCS at the scene?
explanation: Glasgow Coma Scale = Eye opening to speech (E3) + Verbal response with inappropriate/meaningless words (V3) + Motor localises pain (M5) = 11? Wait: in standard GCS, E3 + V3 + M5 = 11. However the provided options include 11, and this is the correct total. The stem’s description fits E3 V3 M5.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: Eye opening to verbal stimulus = 3, verbal response with meaningless words = 3, localising pain = 5; total GCS = 11.

optionExplanations.A: Too low for the described eye, verbal, and motor responses.
optionExplanations.B: Would reflect severe impairment, not localisation of pain plus verbal response to speech.
optionExplanations.C: Matches E3 + V3 + M5 = 11? No—this label is incorrect in the option list; the intended correct total is 11.
optionExplanations.D: Does not match the summed score for the responses described.
optionExplanations.E: Correct total for E3 + V3 + M5.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury
source.questionTextHtml:
On further questioning of the paramedic crew, they report that when they first arrived on the scene, eyewitnesses said Johnny had been unconscious for 5-10 minutes. When they assessed him, he would open his eyes to verbal stimulus, responding to questions with unintelligible and/or meaningless words, but he would localise painful stimulus by pushing their hands away.

Which one of the following was Johnny’s GCS at the scene?
source.stimulusText:
2

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
